target.build: default Go build; Go runtime slice-bounds check is the oracle

classification.vuln_type: slice-bounds-OOB (Go runtime panic, mandatory value absent)

trigger.message: PFCP Heartbeat Request with Recovery Time Stamp IE length mutated to 0
trigger.field: Recovery Time Stamp IE header (type=0x0060) and length (0x0000) are syntactically valid, but the IE does NOT carry the mandatory 4-byte timestamp value required by spec. go-pfcp's IE-specific UnmarshalBinary hardcodes a 4-byte read on the empty payload slice without first checking that the mandatory value is present -> slice bounds out of range panic. PA2 'Absent Field' — exact match to PA2 (2): 'An element whose header and length are syntactically valid does not actually carry the mandatory field values required by the protocol specification.' Distinct from PA1: parser does not USE the length=0 for a mem op; it ignores the declared length and reads the mandatory value assuming presence.
trigger.precondition: None — Heartbeat Request is processed pre-association; the PoC sends Association Setup first only for symmetry, the crash fires on the Heartbeat alone.

ground_truth.crash_type: panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range

root_cause.note: Issue body confirms the Recovery Time Stamp IE length=0 is the trigger but does not include the panic stack. Crash frame inferred to be the IE-specific (*RecoveryTimeStamp).UnmarshalBinary which reads the 4-byte timestamp without checking the IE payload length. Generic dispatch (*IE).UnmarshalBinary in ie.go is the caller.
